title: Every guard refusal and ask names an allowed way out, and a test proves each one is allowed
why: guard_core.refuse() takes a free-text reason, and no check requires a way out. Agents stall or route around a guard when its refusal gives none. Harm stopped: hours of stalled lanes and guessed workarounds. Sighting 04:04 CST Nov 14 (classifier refusals tonight, three, relayed; not read by triage): the auto-mode classifier refused (1) the #3394 record write, (2) and (3) the role split of the #3238 cost-helper move at 03:38 and 03:58 CST as "Undermining Oversight". No refusal named an allowed way out, so lanes asked the owner. Owner item 829 now carries the way out (his hand move or a typed grant). Evidence for this step: a refusal that reads a legal role split as a bypass should say which act is allowed.
note: Owner grant, 09:16 CST Nov 11 ("yes file it for stage 3"; relayed by the coordinator 09:17). Stage 3, beside plan item 3.6 (the guard cull). File only; no build under the freeze. Rough count on main: 21 'Remedy:' lines in hooks/guard.py against about 121 refuse or ask sites (unmeasured exactly; some sites build the remedy elsewhere). The Stop guard's remedy test (lint/test_report_guard_remedy.py) covers only the paths it has fixtures for. Shape: every refusal and ask carries a Remedy that names an allowed act, and a test runs each remedy through the guard to prove it is allowed (generalize the wait-until remedy test in hooks/test_guard.py). The remedy never names the forbidden target (rule git-remedy-never-names-target). Incidents: lanes 2YRQ and 4VY5 stalled for hours on scratchpad-owner asks (Nov 10). The Stop 'Recovered guard' (lint/report_guard.py) refused the coordinator's report three times at 09:1x CST Nov 11, though each report held a Recovered line: the line sat after 'OTHER:' or inside a Done item, and the refusal never says the line must open its own bullet. Triage's own reports hit the same guard twice tonight. Incident 2026-11-11 about 10:00 CST: guard rule scratchpad-owner asked the owner (a permission box) when a triage agent wrote `git show 90c05facc:merge/merge.py` over another agent's scratchpad file. Fix lane scratchpad-owner-refuse (coordinator 10:01 CST): a refusal that names a fresh file name, so no box reaches the owner. Sibling for the 3.6 guard cull (coordinator 10:53 CST Nov 11): in excel-ui-kit session d358e6f5 at about 10:10 CST a sonnet builder was refused an Edit of toolchain/run_chain_selftest.py as a test path, then wrote it through a shell or Python script that was not refused (it restored the file and committed nothing). Decision builders-cannot-edit-tests has a shell check (_shell_write_hit, interpreter_write_hit); one write form or path rule slips it (candidates: PowerShell Set-Content, Python Path.write_text). Exact command unknown; a fix lane only once it is known. Command known (coordinator 10:55 CST, owner relay 10:52): the builder wrote local/ed/r14.py (not a test path) calling Ed('toolchain/run_chain_selftest.py').done(); the open-for-write sits in an imported helper, local/ed/edhelp.py, and Bash ran `python -P local/ed/r14.py`. No command or script scan can follow imports; commit, push and stop still refuse it. The real mistake: the builder routed around a refusal. The builder-test-edit remedy should say plainly: do not write the test by another route; report the needed test change to your orchestrator, who hands it to a test-author. Optional idea for the cull: a builder-only check after each Bash call that reads the working tree for an own test-path change (cost per call unmeasured). False alarms, 2026-11-11 (triage): gh-write-cloud refused three Bash calls in which the shell ready command appeared only as text: triage's roadmap commit of a step file (11:5x CST), and two builder commands on lane ci-wake-mcp-ready (PR #2593, about 12:10 CST). None was a GitHub write. The guard should match a gh command word, not the text inside an argument or a heredoc.
